text:
Yegor Sharangovich's season has drawn the same verdict from the fantasy wires, RotoWire and CBS Sports both running "Still struggling to take next step." Six goals and 12 points in 26 games for a Calgary team that lost six of his last ten won't change many minds.

Our numbers are kinder. Calgary has scored 6.2 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him points, and that usually swings back. His own chances are up a bit from last season (0.96 expected goals per 60 against 0.86), and his finishing is normal. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credited him with clean breakouts last season, 71% of his exits leaving the zone with the puck.

The five-on-five picture is split. The Flames win the shot attempts with him on (54%) but lose the expected goals (46%), so the chances against are dangerous ones. That echoes Evolving-Hockey's verdict last season, near replacement level overall.

He had a power-play goal against Chicago and played almost 24 minutes against Ottawa. Whether the next step comes at 28 is an open question; points he's owed usually show up.
headline: Sharangovich's season is better than it looks
